evidence: far_history_cdc_copy_qm0_v1 selected 584,693 exact matches covering 64,526,086 bytes; canonical command fields cost 4,058,323 bytes but the collective entropy of chronological target gaps, distances, and lengths has not been measured.
hypothesis: QM0 far-history matches average about 110 copied bytes per command, so delta-target, distance, and length fields may have enough collective regularity that one deterministic compressed side ledger preserves more than the 4,389,323-byte target debt after source and reserve.
interfaces_exposed: Canonical 1G raw corpus -> deterministic exact far-copy cover -> one compressed chronological gap/distance/length side ledger; residual payload economics remain a proxy.
kill_condition: Retire the exact collective side-ledger realization without codec integration or parameter sweeps if net average-rate-equivalent gain is below 5,000,000 bytes, repeat ledgers differ, any source proof fails, or any third is empty.
promotion_condition: On exact full 1G, two independently emitted chronological ledgers are byte-identical; LZMA-compressed gap/distance/length records plus compressed source leave at least 5,000,000 average-rate-equivalent bytes, every corpus third contributes copied material, and all sources remain exact, prior, and fully closed.
retired_neighborhoods: Does not reopen QM0 anchor or threshold parameters; differs only by replacing per-command canonical fields with a single collective paid description.
title: Full-1G far-history collective ledger entropy gate
